policy: desk ruling 2026-09-09, standing for both lanes: a delivery enters a fold only at a recorded re-price -- new population file, new arms.json, gate re-read, ledger row. The serve never races the harvest.
ranking_months_are_not_pinned: the 2026 blocks are the serve's target, not a priced fold table; they are rebuilt from whatever the harvest has delivered and their key is not gated. The serve records their population and diffs it against the previous serve's (analysis/ranking-population.json), so a delivery that changes a served file is stated rather than silent -- it is never a stop by itself
read_by: block._summary_path (every summary read and every cache key goes through it), via arms.block_cache_key and arms.month_block
the_pin_is_a_WHITELIST: `airport_days` is the whole of what a pinned month may read. A day that is not named is OUT whether or not it existed when the pin was written, so a delivery landing after the pin is held out with no further action. `dropped_days` is a note of which days were deliberately excluded from the snapshot that built this file, not the mechanism -- the mechanism is the whitelist. Round 5 FALLBACK finding 4: 2025-08-01 landed at 00:28:51 UTC, 65 seconds after this file was first written and six minutes before the v16 serve, and was held out by the whitelist without being named anywhere; it is named now.
what: the airport-day population each FOLD month is pinned to: the set its block was priced on. Pricing, the gates, the dry run and the serve all read this set, so a delivery landing between the price and the serve cannot change what a candidate was gated on
